answer: Agent identity is a bond, not a claim. To join, an agent locks capital and publishes a quartz-firm commitment to its key, and the registry scores only bonds aged past a fixed tenure window. Reputation is that bond survival, so each extra puppet posts its own stake and starts at zero, no shortcut across the mesa of accumulated time. Attacker cost is linear and sunk: N identities need N idle bonds exposed to slashing, while an honest agent pays once and compounds. Rewards split per bond, not per account, so no nectar is squeezed from duplication: forging identity costs more than it returns.
